Optifit

Source: R/cluster.R
optifit.Rd

Optifit is the 'cluster.fit' command in mothur. It allows you to fit sequences to OTUs or existing OTUS. Just like mothur, there are two ways of running this command: open, or closed. Closed fits reads into existing OTUs, and scraps any reads that cannot be fitted(default it closed). Open fits reads into existing OTUs while unfitted OTUs are clustered into new OTUs.

Usage

optifit(
  fit_dist,
  cutoff,
  feature_column_name = "feature",
  bin_column_name = "bin",
  accnos = NULL,
  ref_fasta = NULL,
  ref_count = NULL,
  ref_list = NULL,
  fit_fasta = NULL,
  fit_percent = 50,
  closed = FALSE,
  print_ref = TRUE,
  random_seed = 123,
  max_iterations = 100,
  denovo_iters = 10,
  optimal_denovo_result = TRUE,
  ref_weight = "none",
  metric = "mcc",
  pairwise_distance_method = "onegap",
  number_of_threads = 1,
  strollur_object = NULL
)

Arguments

fit_dist

The distance object that will be used to fit to the new reference. This must be created using the `read_dist()` function.

cutoff

The cutoff you want to cluster towards.

feature_column_name

Set the name of the column in the cluster dataframe that contains the sequence names. This is a `character` value.

bin_column_name

Set the name of the column in the cluster dataframe that contains the name of the group of sequence names. This is a `character` value.

accnos

a `vector` of strings that represent the reference sequences by name. Use this when you know the group of sequences you want your fit data to fit against.

ref_fasta

a`data.frame` representation of your fasta data for your reference sequences. This can be generated using the `read_fasta()` function. The fasta `data.frame` must contain two columns: "sequence_name" and "sequence."

ref_count

a `data.frame` that display sequence abundance for the reference sequences. Must be generated using the `read_count()` function.

ref_list

a `data.frame` respentation of the mothur list file you wish to fit your sequences to. Can be generated using the `read_mothur_list()` function. Must include two columns: "bin_name" and "sequence_name."

fit_fasta

a`data.frame` representation of your fasta data for your fitted sequences. This can be generated using the `read_fasta()` function. The fasta `data.frame` must contain two columns: "sequence_name" and "sequence."

fit_percent

allows you to set the percentage of reads that need to be fitted. This is a `numerical` value.

closed

deteremines whether you want the function to run using the closed or open method. The closed method will return reads that fit into existing otus and scrap those that did not. The open method will keep reads that fit into existing otus and create new OTUs for those that did not. This is a `logical` value.

print_ref

controls whether all the reference sequences are printed in the final result. This is a `character` value.

random_seed

a `integer` value that represents the current random seed.

max_iterations

the max number of iterations that cluster computes. This is a `integer` value.

denovo_iters

the max number of iterations the denovo method computes. This is a `integer` value.

optimal_denovo_result

determines whether or not you want the denovo method to return the cluster with the highest mcc value or all of the randomly computed clusters. This is a `logical` value.

ref_weight

Ref Weight is used to randomize the reference sequences for the denovo method. There are three methods: none, abundance and connectivity. "none" will do a normal shuffle of the given sequences without any weights, abundance will shuffle the sequences using abundances as a weight, and connectivity will shuffle the sequences but uses a weight of one for every sequence.

metric

this parameter allows you to choose which metric the cluster will optimize to, the options are: Matthews correlation coefficient (mcc), sensitivity (sens), specificity (spec), true positives + true negatives (tptn), false positives + false negatives (fpfn), true positives (tp), true negative (tn), false positive (fp), false negative (fn), f1score (f1score), accuracy (accuracy), positive predictive value (ppv), negative predictive value (npv), false discovery rate (fdr). The default metric is mcc.

pairwise_distance_method

the method you wish to use to calculate pairwise distances between aligned sequences. As of current we only allow the calculation of fasta sequences, and the current methods are; onegap, nogap, and eachgap. For more information look at the (mother webpage)[https://mothur.org/wiki/dist.seqs/]. This is a `character` value.

number_of_threads

a `integer` value that represents the amount of allotted threads that can be used.

strollur_object

Using the `strollur` r package, you can use your created strollur object to save your clustering results to. This allows you to seamless modify your strollur object and analysis results as needed.

Value

A `list` of a list of `data.frames` that contain abundance, and clustering results. If you used `method = opticlust`, it will also return clustering performance metrics.

Examples

 amazon_count <- read_count(example_path("amazon.full.count_table"))
 amazon_dist <- read_dist(example_path("amazon_phylip.dist"),
                          amazon_count, 0.03)

 esophagus_fasta <- read_fasta(example_path("esophagus.fasta"))
 esophagus_count <- read_count(example_path("esophagus.count_table"))
 amazon_fasta <- read_fasta(example_path("amazon.align"))
 esophagus_list <- read_mothur_list(example_path("esophagus.list"))


 denovo <- optifit(amazon_dist, 0.03)
#> accnos, ref_fasta, ref_count, ref_list, and fit_fastaparameters are all NULL. Running Optifit using denovo.
 denovo_open <- optifit(amazon_dist, 0.03, close = FALSE)
#> accnos, ref_fasta, ref_count, ref_list, and fit_fastaparameters are all NULL. Running Optifit using denovo.
 accnos <- optifit(amazon_dist, 0.03,
                   accnos = amazon_count$Representative_Sequence[1:40])
#> Accnos file is not null, running optifit using accnos.
 accnos_open <- optifit(amazon_dist, 0.03,
                        accnos = amazon_count$Representative_Sequence[1:40],
                        closed=FALSE)
#> Accnos file is not null, running optifit using accnos.

 ref_cluster <- optifit(amazon_dist, 0.03, "feature", "bin", accnos = NULL,
                        ref_fasta = esophagus_fasta,
                        ref_count = esophagus_count,
                        ref_list = esophagus_list, fit_fasta = amazon_fasta,
                        pairwise_distance_method = "onegap",
                        number_of_threads = parallel::detectCores(),
                        print_ref = TRUE)
#> ref_fasta, ref_list, ref_count, and fit_fasta are not NULL, running reference based optifit.
